production.note: US model years. First: the 2015 press kit says "The 600-horsepower GT-R NISMO joins the established 2015 GT-R Premium and GT-R Black Edition vehicles"; Nissan's reveal (nissan-global-2013-gt-r-nismo-reveal) put US sales 'later in 2014'. Last: the 2024 press kit (nissan-us-2024-gt-r-press-kit) lists the 2024 GT-R NISMO and says "GT-R production for the North American market will sunset in October". Whether a Nismo was sold in every model year in between was not checked.

body.note: Inferred from Nissan's description: a two-door car with 'Capacity 4 passengers'. No opened Nissan US page uses the word coupe.

displacementL.note: Nissan's US specification tables give litres only: 'Displacement (liters) 3.8'. No cc figure for the Nismo was found on an opened Nissan page.

drivetrain.note: 'Mid-mounted front engine / rear transaxle ATTESA E-TS all-wheel drive'

powerHp.note: Quote: "Horsepower 600 HP @ 6,800 RPM" (GT-R NISMO, 2023; same in the 2024 kit). Unchanged since launch: the 2015 press kit gives "600 horsepower @ 6,800 rpm, 481 lb-ft of torque @ 3,200 - 5,800 rpm" (nissan-us-2015-gt-r-press-kit). The reference year is 2023 rather than 2015 because the 2015 to 2020 press kits opened give no curb weight for the Nismo.

weightLb.note: GT-R NISMO, 2023 model year. Quote: "Curb weight (pounds) Front 2,119 Rear 1,748 Total 3,867"; the 2024 kit repeats it (nissan-us-2024-gt-r-press-kit). No Nissan curb weight for the 2015 to 2019 Nismo was found.
